With just weeks to go before the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Fold launch, Apple is bustling behind the scenes. According to a new report from Bloomberg, Apple is holding a lottery for its U.S. retail employees to select staff to travel to California to help prepare for the iPhone launch event in September.

iPhone launch event scheduled for September

The report states that Apple Store retail employees can apply to take part in iPhone launch event work, with duties including "helping organize crowd queues, registering attendees, hosting guests, providing directions, and supporting the security team."

Apple announced the lottery in an internal memo today, and said the event would be held in the first half of September.

Apple said in the memo that it was "excited to be able to offer U.S. store team members the opportunity to participate in an event-support experience program." For years, Apple has relied on retail employees to help coordinate major product launches. Employees who took part in this year's Worldwide Developers Conference or last year's iPhone launch event are not eligible to apply for this program. According to the memo, applicants must submit their applications by August 8, and Apple will notify those selected on August 17.

Apple traditionally holds its annual iPhone launch event in the second week of September. With U.S. Labor Day falling on September 7 this year, Bloomberg noted that "a Wednesday event is slightly more likely, since that preserves the workday travel window Apple has historically offered attendees."

If everything goes as expected, the iPhone launch event will be held on Wednesday, September 9. Pre-orders are expected to open that Friday, with the official on-sale date one week later.
